name: derivation_thresholds
description: Version 4 (Story 3.1): version 3's twelve parameters unchanged, plus the one the indemnity-type derivation reads. Superseding is a new document, never an edit — v1, v2 and v3 stay exactly what Stories 2.1, 2.2 and 2.5 shipped, so an ordering, a banner or a forms card produced under any of them is still explainable. ptdSeverityThreshold is the severity score at or above which a permanently disabled worker is treated as permanently TOTALLY disabled rather than partially: it decides the indemnity type (ptd vs ppd) and, through it, the comp rate the weekly benefit is computed at. It lives in THIS document rather than in benefit_params because indemnity_type is a registered derivation (AD-10) and DerivationThresholds is the single argument every registered derivation is built from — the same argument v3 made for the path parameters. The split matters more here than it did there: the PTD test is asked ONCE, of the derivation, and services/financials consumes its answer rather than re-deriving it, so this threshold has exactly one reader and AD-8's 'each rule element in exactly one tier' is a fact about the code rather than a convention. The rate the PTD branch then pays (ptdCompRateBp) is financial tuning and lives in benefit_params, which services/financials owns. 85 is the prototype's cut-off (computeBenefit: c.disability==="Permanent" && c.sevScore>=85), ported exactly.
